jurisdiction.name: Uzbekistan
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Uzbekistan governs AI mainly through presidential acts led by the Ministry of Digital Technologies: the 2021 AI programme (PQ-4996), the AI Development Strategy to 2030 (PQ-358, 2024) with targets revised in 2026, and 2025 decrees on priority AI projects, funding and fast-track procurement. Since 2026 these are backed by statutory rules: Law ZRU-1115 defines AI, bars decisions affecting rights from resting solely on AI output and fines unlawful AI processing of personal data, the ministry's AI Ethics Rules are binding from June 2026, and a September 2026 cabinet resolution created an AI procurement register. The 2019 personal data law also applies.
lead_institutions: President of the Republic of Uzbekistan
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. All records were read on the official legal portal; central bank AI rules required by the strategy have not been published and are listed as leads.

instruments.official_title: «Рақамли Ўзбекистон-2030» стратегиясини тасдиқлаш ва уни самарали амалга ошириш чора-тадбирлари тўғрисида
instruments.english_title: On approval of the 'Digital Uzbekistan-2030' Strategy and measures for its effective implementation (Presidential Decree PF-6079)
instruments.issuing_authority: President of the Republic of Uzbekistan
instruments.current_status: In force as amended; most recently amended by Presidential Decree PF-141 of 24 July 2026, which aligns its digital and AI targets with the 'Uzbekistan-2030' strategy. Signed 5 October 2020.
instruments.summary: Presidential Decree PF-6079 approves the 'Digital Uzbekistan-2030' strategy and sets up a Coordination Commission chaired by the Prime Minister to implement it. The strategy covers digital infrastructure, e-government, the digital economy and IT education, and includes tasks on introducing AI, machine learning and big-data technologies in economic sectors and on implementing AI projects; it is the stated basis of the later AI resolutions PQ-4996 and PQ-358.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Umbrella national digital strategy with an AI pillar; its Coordination Commission oversees AI programmes and funding.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full text on lex.uz (National Database of Legislation, run by the Ministry of Justice's 'Adolat' National Legal Information Centre) read; decree text and annexes checked for AI provisions (23 mentions of AI); first official publication 06.10.2020 (No. 06/20/6079/1349) and entry into force 06.10.2020 per the lex.uz record. Issuing act details: President of the Republic of Uzbekistan (Decree PF-6079 of 5 October 2020).

instruments.official_title: Сунъий интеллект технологияларини жадал жорий этиш учун шарт-шароитлар яратиш чора-тадбирлари тўғрисида
instruments.english_title: On measures to create conditions for the accelerated introduction of artificial intelligence technologies (Presidential Resolution PQ-4996)
instruments.issuing_authority: President of the Republic of Uzbekistan
instruments.current_status: In force as amended (amendments published 29.07.2021, 15.04.2022, 31.08.2022, 03.12.2022, 04.01.2024, 07.04.2026 by Decree PF-54 and 13.04.2026). Signed 17 February 2021. Its 2021-2022 programme has been followed by the AI Development Strategy to 2030 (PQ-358), but the resolution itself has not been repealed.
instruments.summary: Uzbekistan's first AI-specific act: it approves a 2021-2022 programme of measures to study and introduce AI, including drafting an AI development strategy and uniform requirements, liability, safety and transparency rules for developing and using AI in the economy, social sphere and public administration. It assigns pilot AI projects to named ministries (agriculture, banking, finance, tax, transport, energy, health, pharmaceuticals, e-government Face-ID), lists open government data for AI projects, creates a Research Institute for the Development of Digital Technologies and AI and an AI department in the ICT ministry, and launches AI degree programmes.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Founding AI governance act: sets the first AI programme, institutions and ministry pilot assignments.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full text on lex.uz (National Database of Legislation, run by the Ministry of Justice's 'Adolat' National Legal Information Centre) read; operative paragraphs 1-7 and annex list read; official publication 18.02.2021 (No. 07/21/4996/0127) and entry into force 18.02.2021 per the lex.uz record. Issuing act details: President of the Republic of Uzbekistan (Resolution PQ-4996 of 17 February 2021).

instruments.official_title: Сунъий интеллект технологияларини 2030 йилга қадар ривожлантириш стратегиясини тасдиқлаш тўғрисида
instruments.english_title: On approval of the Strategy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence Technologies until 2030 (Presidential Resolution PQ-358)
instruments.issuing_authority: President of the Republic of Uzbekistan
instruments.current_status: Adopted and being implemented; amended by Decrees PF-189 (22 Oct 2025), PF-223 (Nov 2025) and PF-141 (24 Jul 2026). Signed 14 October 2024; the lex.uz record gives 17 October 2024 as publication and entry-into-force date. A Russian translation (unofficial) is on lex.uz at https://lex.uz/docs/7158606.
instruments.summary: Approves the national AI Development Strategy to 2030 with targets including USD 1.5 billion of AI-based software and services, 10% of services on the Single Portal of Interactive Public Services delivered with AI, and a top-50 place in the Government AI Readiness Index. It approves a 2024-2026 action plan and a list of 'big data' sets that ministries must provide (in compliance with personal data law, including in anonymised form), sets priority AI uses in banking, tax and customs, health, agriculture and energy, and makes the Minister of Digital Technologies personally responsible for implementation under the Digital Uzbekistan-2030 Coordination Commission.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national AI strategy and action plan.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full text on lex.uz (National Database of Legislation, run by the Ministry of Justice's 'Adolat' National Legal Information Centre) read; Uzbek official text header and Russian lex.uz translation (doc 7158606) operative paragraphs 1-12 read; official publication 17.10.2024 (No. 07/24/358/0825) and entry into force 17.10.2024 per lex.uz. Issuing act details: President of the Republic of Uzbekistan (Resolution PQ-358 of 14 October 2024).

instruments.english_title: On measures to implement priority projects in the field of artificial intelligence technologies in 2025-2026 (Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 425)
instruments.issuing_authority: Cabinet of Ministers of the Republic of Uzbekistan
instruments.current_status: In force; amended by a 2026 Cabinet resolution (published 21.07.2026). Signed 10 July 2025.
instruments.summary: Implements PQ-358 by reorganising the Ministry of Digital Technologies' Digital Economy Research Centre into a 'Centre for the Development of AI and the Digital Economy'. It approves lists of priority AI projects for 2025-2026 to be carried out by organisations of the Ministry of Digital Technologies (funded from the Reconstruction and Development Fund) and by other ministries and agencies, which must report quarterly to the Ministry on progress.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Creates the national AI centre and binds ministries to deliver listed AI projects.

instruments.official_title: Сунъий интеллект технологияларини янада ривожлантиришга оид қўшимча чора-тадбирлар тўғрисида
instruments.english_title: On additional measures for the further development of artificial intelligence technologies (Presidential Decree PF-189)
instruments.issuing_authority: President of the Republic of Uzbekistan
instruments.current_status: In force. Signed 22 October 2025. Implemented by the Ministry of Digital Technologies' AI Ethics Rules (2026) and Cabinet Resolution No. 510 (2026) on the AI procurement register.
instruments.summary: Sets goals of at least 100 AI projects in government, social and economic sectors by end-2026, over USD 1 billion of foreign investment in AI infrastructure by 2030, AI in school and university curricula from 2026/2027 and 15 university AI labs. From 1 January 2026 draft legal acts and technical specifications providing for AI must be agreed with the National Agency for Perspective Projects, which also sets procedures for AI in crypto-assets, e-commerce, insurance and securities; it creates an AI alliance, the ai.gov.uz portal, a GPU-access centre, a ministerial AI ranking, and from 1 June 2026 simplified direct-contract procurement of registered AI systems up to 2,500 base calculation units.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Main operative AI decree: institutional set-up, sector oversight role for the National Agency for Perspective Projects and AI procurement fast-track.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full text on lex.uz (National Database of Legislation, run by the Ministry of Justice's 'Adolat' National Legal Information Centre) read; sections I-III read in full; official publication 27.10.2025 (No. 06/25/189/0978), entry into force 27.10.2025 per lex.uz. Issuing act details: President of the Republic of Uzbekistan (Decree PF-189 of 22 October 2025).

instruments.official_title: Sunʼiy intellekt texnologiyalariga asoslangan loyihalarni qoʻllab-quvvatlashga oid qoʻshimcha chora-tadbirlar toʻgʻrisida
instruments.english_title: On additional measures to support projects based on artificial intelligence technologies (Presidential Resolution PQ-320)
instruments.issuing_authority: President of the Republic of Uzbekistan
instruments.summary: Allocates an additional USD 100 million from the Reconstruction and Development Fund for 2026-2027: USD 50 million in grants for introducing AI in state bodies (priority to socially significant projects) and USD 50 million to the 'Fund of Funds' and 'IT Park Ventures' for AI start-ups. Funds are distributed by the Digital Uzbekistan-2030 Coordination Commission, with state bodies submitting AI proposals by 1 December 2025; it also finances creation of the ai.gov.uz national portal.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Funding mechanism for public-sector AI adoption and AI start-ups.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full text on lex.uz (National Database of Legislation, run by the Ministry of Justice's 'Adolat' National Legal Information Centre) read; sections I-II and paragraph 4 read; official publication 31.10.2025 (No. 07/25/320/0998), entry into force 31.10.2025 per lex.uz. instruments.official_title: Сунъий интеллектни қўллаш орқали юзага келадиган муносабатлар тартибга солиниши муносабати билан Ўзбекистон Республикасининг айрим қонун ҳужжатларига қўшимча ва ўзгартиришлар киритиш тўғрисида
instruments.english_title: On making additions and changes to certain legislative acts of the Republic of Uzbekistan in connection with the regulation of relations arising from the use of artificial intelligence (Law ZRU-1115)
instruments.issuing_authority: Oliy Majlis of the Republic of Uzbekistan
instruments.current_status: In force from 21 January 2026 (official publication). Earlier media reports of a mandatory AI-content labelling duty refer to the draft bill; the enacted text read on lex.uz contains no labelling provision. English (https://lex.uz/docs/8011930) and Russian (https://lex.uz/docs/8011377) translations on lex.uz are unofficial.
instruments.summary: Amends the Law on Informatization to define 'artificial intelligence', add AI development to state policy and the authorised body's powers, and insert Article 7-1: AI-created information resources and AI-based information systems must not harm a person's life, health, freedom, honour, dignity or other rights, and legally significant decisions affecting human rights and freedoms may not be based solely on the conclusions of AI-based systems. It also adds to Article 46-2 of the Code of Administrative Liability a fine of 50-100 base calculation units, with confiscation, for unlawful processing of personal data using AI and its dissemination in media, telecom networks or the internet.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Uzbekistan's first statutory AI rules: legal AI definition, harm and no-sole-reliance rules, and an AI-specific personal-data offence.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full text on lex.uz (National Database of Legislation, run by the Ministry of Justice's 'Adolat' National Legal Information Centre) read; Uzbek official text header and publication note read; full Russian translation (lex.uz doc 8011377) Articles 1-4 read; official publication 21.01.2026 (No. 03/26/1115/0063); in force from official publication (Article 4). Issuing act details: Oliy Majlis of the Republic of Uzbekistan (adopted by the Legislative Chamber 12 August 2025, approved by the Senate 1 November 2025); signed by the President 21 January 2026.

instruments.official_title: Сунъий интеллектга асосланган ечимларни яратиш, жорий қилиш ва улардан фойдаланиш бўйича этика қоидаларини тасдиқлаш тўғрисида
instruments.english_title: On approval of the Ethics Rules for the creation, implementation and use of AI-based solutions (Order of the Minister of Digital Technologies, registered by the Ministry of Justice No. 3787)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Digital Technologies of the Republic of Uzbekistan (Order of the Minister)
instruments.current_status: Registered 14 March 2026, published 16 March 2026, in force since 17 June 2026.
instruments.summary: Ministerial order, issued under PF-189 and PQ-358 and agreed with the Supreme Court, Ministry of Internal Affairs, State Security Service, Anti-Corruption Agency and National Agency for Perspective Projects, approving Ethics Rules for AI-based solutions. The rules bind 'AI participants' (developers, implementers and users) to eight principles: legality; priority of protecting the person, society, state and environment; understandability; responsibility, accountability and control; fairness and non-discrimination; openness and transparency; data protection; and reliability and safety, and set out the participants' rights and obligations.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First national AI ethics code, issued as a registered normative act.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full text on lex.uz (National Database of Legislation, run by the Ministry of Justice's 'Adolat' National Legal Information Centre) read; order and Chapter 2 principles read; official publication 16.03.2026 (No. 10/26/3787/0237); entry into force three months after publication (17.06.2026) per paragraph 2 and the lex.uz record. Issuing act details: Ministry of Digital Technologies of the Republic of Uzbekistan (Order of the Minister; registered by the Ministry of Justice on 14 March 2026, No. 3787).

instruments.english_title: On amendments and additions to certain documents of the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan in connection with further improvement of strategic planning and state control in the field of digital technologies (Presidential Decree PF-141)
instruments.issuing_authority: President of the Republic of Uzbekistan
instruments.current_status: In force. Signed 24 July 2026; amends PQ-358 and PF-6079.
instruments.summary: Amends the Digital Uzbekistan-2030 decree (PF-6079), the AI Development Strategy to 2030 (PQ-358) and other presidential acts to align digital and AI targets with the 'Uzbekistan-2030' strategy. It sets a goal of training 5 million young people under the 'Five Million AI Leaders' project by 2030 and strengthens state control over information, mass communications, telecoms, digital technologies and publishing.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Latest revision of the AI strategy targets and governance arrangements.

instruments.english_title: On approval of the Regulation on the procedure for forming and maintaining the register of AI-based information systems (software products) of business entities permitted for public procurement by request for quotation (Cabinet of Ministers Resolution No. 510)
instruments.issuing_authority: Cabinet of Ministers of the Republic of Uzbekistan
instruments.current_status: In force since 23 September 2026; the register itself is due to launch by 1 February 2027. Signed 22 September 2026.
instruments.summary: Implements PF-189 by approving a regulation on a single register of businesses and their AI-based information systems that state bodies, majority state-owned companies and local authorities may buy by request for quotation up to 2,500 base calculation units. Technical specifications of registered systems are reviewed by the Cybersecurity Centre and the Digital Government Projects Management Centre, in agreement with the National Agency for Perspective Projects, to check security, transparency and quality requirements, and the list of registered systems is published on the ai.gov.uz national portal; the register must be launched by 1 February 2027.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: AI-specific public procurement rule with security and transparency vetting.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full text on lex.uz (National Database of Legislation, run by the Ministry of Justice's 'Adolat' National Legal Information Centre) read; resolution paragraphs 1-4 read; official publication 23.09.2026 (No. 09/26/510/0964), entry into force 23.09.2026 per lex.uz. Issuing act details: Cabinet of Ministers of the Republic of Uzbekistan (Resolution No. 510 of 22 September 2026).

instruments.issuing_authority: Oliy Majlis of the Republic of Uzbekistan
instruments.current_status: In force as amended (latest amendments listed on lex.uz include 2021 and 2023). Signed 2 July 2019.
instruments.summary: Uzbekistan's general personal data law governing collection, processing, storage and transfer of personal data by owners and operators, including registration of personal data databases and rules for automated processing (Article 24). It designates the State Personalisation Centre under the Cabinet of Ministers as the authorised state body for personal data. It governs the personal data used to train and run AI systems; Law ZRU-1115 (2026) added an administrative offence for unlawful AI-based processing of personal data.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law applicable to AI training and use.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full text on lex.uz (National Database of Legislation, run by the Ministry of Justice's 'Adolat' National Legal Information Centre) read; table of contents and Articles 8 and 24 checked; first official publication 03.07.2019 (No. 03/19/547/3363); entry into force 01.10.2019 per lex.uz. Issuing act details: Oliy Majlis of the Republic of Uzbekistan (adopted by the Legislative Chamber 16 April 2019, approved by the Senate 21 June 2019); signed by the President 2 July 2019.

instruments.official_title: Указ Президента Республики Узбекистан от 06.07.2026 г. № УП-123 «О мерах по дальнейшему развитию искусственного интеллекта и цифровизации в деятельности по государственному аудиту»
instruments.english_title: Presidential Decree No. UP-123 of 6 July 2026 on measures to further develop artificial intelligence and digitalisation in state audit
instruments.issuing_authority: President of the Republic of Uzbekistan
instruments.current_status: Published in the National Database of Legislation on 6 July 2026 (No. 06/26/123/0692); entered into force on 6 July 2026.
instruments.summary: Presidential decree setting 2026-2030 goals for using AI in the Accounts Chamber's audit work. From 2027 the Chamber is to audit how AI systems used by government bodies perform and run risk-based IT audits; from 1 September 2028 compliance audits are to use AI. It orders an AI development concept by 1 August 2026, an AI laboratory by 1 December 2026, approves policy principles and a roadmap as annexes, and asks for legislative amendments within three months.

instruments.official_title: Постановление Президента Республики Узбекистан от 26.08.2021 г. № ПП-5234 «О мерах по внедрению Специального режима применения технологий искусственного интеллекта»
instruments.english_title: Presidential Resolution No. PP-5234 of 26 August 2021 on measures to introduce the Special Regime for the application of artificial intelligence technologies
instruments.issuing_authority: President of the Republic of Uzbekistan
instruments.current_status: Published in the National Database of Legislation on 26 August 2021 (No. 07/21/5234/0826); lex.uz shows a later revision dated 23 August 2022. The resolution set the special regime for five years, with extension possible by the Digital Uzbekistan 2030 coordination commission.
instruments.summary: Presidential resolution creating a five-year special regime (regulatory sandbox) for AI pilot projects by IT Park residents. Participants get accelerated permits (five working days), reduced documents and fees, access to depersonalised data and training cost reimbursement; pilots run up to one year, participants must notify clients and keep a testing register, and may get permission for full deployment after successful tests. The ICT ministry is the working body.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Uzbekistan's national legislation database, the drafts portal, the President's and Cabinet's acts, ministries and regulators (the central bank and the personal data, cybersecurity and standards bodies) were searched. No qualifying document was found for cybersecurity, standards, sandboxes, readiness indices, generative AI, drafts, international agreements or historical publications. The drafts portal and the national standards catalogue could not be searched directly, and the annexes of one presidential action plan and whether a separate AI law bill exists still need to be checked.
coverage_audit.technical_note: Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. regulation.gov.uz drafts portal search is browser-only (no AI drafts found via search engines); O'zstandart catalogue not searched directly. PQ-358 annexes only partly read. ZRU-1115 has no AI-content labelling provision (media reports refer to the draft). Not a party to Convention 108. Units covered: Law: lex.uz searched (Uzbek, Russian, English titles): AI amendments law ZRU-1115 (2026) and Personal Data Law ZRU-547 recorded; enacted law contains no AI labelling or deepfake offence; no stand-alone AI law or pending AI bill text found; regulation.gov.uz draft search is script-driven and returned no AI drafts via search.; Government: President (PF-6079, PQ-4996, PQ-358, PF-189, PQ-320, PF-141) and Cabinet of Ministers (No. 425, No. 510) acts recorded; Ministry of Digital Technologies AI page on gov.uz checked.; Ministries: Ministry of Digital Technologies AI Ethics Rules (No. 3787) recorded; searched for education, health, justice/courts, internal affairs AI orders on lex.uz: nothing AI-specific found beyond ministry project assignments inside PQ-4996, PQ-358 and No. 425. Cabinet Resolution No. 288 (2026) on the President's AI Award start-up contest seen but not recorded (award procedure, not governance).; Regulators: Central Bank (cbu.uz): no AI regulation or guidance found (lead). Personal data authority (State Personalisation Centre): no AI guidance found. National Agency for Perspective Projects: AI procedures required by PF-189 not found (lead). Cybersecurity Centre: role in AI procurement vetting via No. 510 only; no AI security guidance found. Standards (O'zstandart): no national adoption of ISO/IEC 42001 or other AI standard found.. Not reached: regulation.gov.uz drafts portal (dynamic search page; no AI drafts surfaced via search engines); O'zstandart standards catalogue not directly searched. Could not verify: Annex contents of PQ-358 (2024-2026 action plan) only partly read; Whether a separate comprehensive 'Law on Artificial Intelligence' bill exists (mentioned only in academic sources). cyber-security, standards, sandbox, index-readiness, generative-ai, drafts, international, historical: no material found. Weekly change check 2026-10-22: lex.uz loads (search page is JavaScript-driven, so web search of lex.uz titles was used); no new AI-governing act since the 2026-10-12 review. NAPP (PF-189 para 3b) and Central Bank AI items still not found; regulation.gov.uz drafts portal not searchable without a browser.
